meta.title: Wedding & party photo games: 10 QR code ideas for guests
meta.description: Photo game ideas for weddings, birthdays, baptisms and parties: simple challenges to run with the MIOLOVE QR code so your guests take real, spontaneous photos.
meta.ogTitle: 10 ways to get guests taking photos with the MIOLOVE QR code

hero.sub: Wedding, birthday, baptism or just a good party: 10 original ideas to turn the album's QR code into a game that gets more photos, and better ones, from the people who are there.
hero.note: No app for guests. No game engine: the album's own features are enough.

concept.title: What is a QR photo game?
concept.p1: The album's QR code usually ends up as a card on the table: a few people scan it and then forget about it. A photo game gives it a reason to be used: a small challenge, a theme, a table-versus-table contest that invites everyone to look around and take a picture.
concept.p2: There is nothing new to set up. Guests scan the QR code, send photos and videos from their phone without signing up, and you see everything in the album and on the big screen. You decide the game, in words: on the card, over the microphone, on a note at each table.
concept.note: These are ideas and practical tips, not fixed rules: pick the one that suits you and adapt it to your event.

steps.title: How it works, in 3 steps
steps.sub: From idea to the first photo in under a minute per guest.

s1.d: Choose the challenge that fits the event and your crowd. A single one, announced well, is enough.

s2.d: Print the MIOLOVE card and add one line with the challenge: “One colour, one photo” or “Moment hunt”.

s3.d: Guests send photos and videos with no app and no account. You find them in the album in original quality, and can show them on the big screen.

list.title: 10 original ideas to get guests shooting
list.sub: For each one you will see how easy it is to run, when it works best and why it makes a difference.

hunt.title: Moment hunt
hunt.text: A list of small moments to catch during the evening: the first toast, someone dancing barefoot, grandparents hugging grandchildren, the cake arriving. Whoever sees the moment, shoots it.
hunt.when: All through the party, announcing the list at the start of the reception.
hunt.why: It gives every guest a concrete task: photos come from exactly the moments nobody would otherwise capture.

tables.title: Table versus table
tables.text: Each table tries to tell the evening its own way. Ask guests to type “Name · Table 4” in the name field and, after dinner, look at which table collected the funniest shots.
tables.when: During dinner, when tables are full and the mood is relaxed.
tables.why: A friendly contest between tables draws in even the shyest guests and makes it easy to see who took what.

beforeAfter.title: Before and after
beforeAfter.text: Ask for two photos of the same place or the same people: at the start of the evening and at the end. The neatly set table and then the wrecked one, the posed group and then the dishevelled one.
beforeAfter.when: Open the game on arrival and close it with the last dance or the cake cutting.
beforeAfter.why: The comparison tells the story of time passing and a party well enjoyed better than words: a tiny story made of two shots.

colour.title: One colour, one photo
colour.text: Pick a colour (say red) and invite everyone to find something of that colour and photograph it creatively. Change colour for every course or every hour.
colour.when: Aperitif, the wait between courses, any moment when people are waiting.
colour.why: It turns photography into an observation game: people look at the room with fresh eyes and find details nobody else noticed.

generations.title: Generations together
generations.text: Invite guests to take a photo with someone of a different age: grandchild and grandmother, little cousin and uncle, a friend and her mum. Each pairing of generations becomes a portrait to keep.
generations.when: After the formal part, once everyone has relaxed and is mixing.
generations.why: The most treasured family photos are between generations, and they usually go missing because nobody thinks to organise them.

details.title: The little details
details.text: Photographers focus on the key moments; guests see the rest. Ask them to photograph details: shoes, hands, the centrepiece, a note, the forgotten glass.
details.when: Before the ceremony, during the set-up or during the reception.
details.why: You get an album full of atmosphere, with small things that bring the day back more than posed big moments do.

emoji.title: Live emoji
emoji.text: Announce one emoji at a time: 😂 a laugh, 😍 a lovestruck look, 🥳 a party face. Guests act it out live and send the shot.
emoji.when: In musical pauses, before dessert, or as a warm-up at the start.
emoji.why: It is instant, funny and works at any age: even people who hate posing enjoy pulling the right face.

angle.title: Unusual angle
angle.text: Ask for photos from an unexpected point of view: from below, from behind, from the top of a chair, reflected in a glass, just shadows or dancing feet.
angle.when: On the dance floor or after dinner, when there is energy and appetite to experiment.
angle.why: Photos that are different from usual are the ones that surprise: you see the party the way guests see it, not as a script.

candid.title: The most candid photo
candid.text: No posing: reward the most genuine shot of the evening, the one where someone laughs without noticing they are being photographed. At the end, choose a winner together.
candid.when: All evening, with a small symbolic prize at the end of the party.
candid.why: Candid photos are the ones people love to look back on, and a goal worth winning encourages guests to hunt for them.

keepsake.title: A keepsake for the guest of honour
keepsake.text: Each guest sends a photo or a short video with a wish, a memory or a piece of advice for the person being celebrated: the couple, the birthday person, the baptised child. You watch it all together later.
keepsake.when: Ask before the party, or collect the messages during the reception.
keepsake.why: It becomes a group gift with no cost or organisation: an album of voices and faces the honoured person will revisit for years.

occasions.title: The right idea for every occasion
occasions.sub: How to adapt the games to each kind of party, with the tips that work best.

wedding.title: Wedding photo games
wedding.text: A wedding has many guests from different circles: games that mix tables and generations work very well. Keep the challenges light so they never take anything away from the ceremony.
wedding.tip: Put the QR code on the table and on the programme card, and announce the game over the microphone after the starter.

birthday.title: Birthday photo games
birthday.text: A birthday needs instant fun: quick challenges, emoji, silly pictures. If the party is for a child, bring the grown-ups in with the keepsake idea for the birthday child.
birthday.tip: Prepare a list of 3 challenges and put it next to the cake, where everyone passes.

baptism.title: Baptism photo ideas
baptism.text: A baptism is a family party: photos across generations, details and a message of good wishes for the little one who will grow up looking at the album all work well.
baptism.tip: Ask the grandparents to start: if they go first, everyone else follows.

other.title: QR albums for parties and other events
other.text: Anniversaries, graduations, hen and stag parties, dinners with friends: any occasion with a group of people can have its shared album and its challenge.
other.tip: Choose one easy challenge and repeat it: one clear thing beats a long list.

benefits.title: Why playing with the QR code makes the album better

b1.t: More photos, from more points of view
b1.d: A challenge gets people who usually do not shoot to take part: the album tells the party through many different eyes.

b2.d: Guests scan the QR code and send. You do not have to explain anything complicated.

b3.d: Photos and videos keep the quality they were shot in, and you can download them all in a single ZIP.

b4.d: No scattered chats or expired links: every memory ends up in the event's album and can appear on the big screen.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the ideas

q1.q: Do I need to set anything up to play?
q1.a: No. The ideas use what the album already does: guests scan the QR code and send photos and videos. You announce the challenge yourself, aloud or on a card, with no extra settings.

q2.q: Do guests have to install an app or sign up?
q2.a: No. It opens on their phone after scanning the QR code, with no app and no account. They can leave a name, but it is optional.

q3.q: How do I tell apart the photos of one table or challenge?
q3.a: Ask guests to type a name like “Julia · Table 4” in the optional name field: you will see it next to each photo in the album.

q4.q: Can I use several ideas at the same party?
q4.a: Of course, but fewer and clearer works better: one challenge at a time, announced at the right moment, beats a long list.

q5.q: Do the ideas work for birthdays, baptisms and other parties too?
q5.a: Yes. Each idea shows which occasions it suits, and this guide has specific tips for weddings, birthdays, baptisms and other events.

q6.a: Yes: you can create a free trial album and see how it works with your guests before activating the full album.

s3.d: They scan the code or open the link, take or pick photos and videos from their camera roll, and send them. A page opens in the browser: no app and no account, grandparents included.

s4.d: Photos reach the album as they are sent. After the christening, with the Full album, you download the originals as one ZIP to save with the family photos.

moments.title: From the church door to the lunch table: where to put the QR code
moments.sub: A christening has its own rhythm: the QR code matters most once the service is over.

m1.d: At church it’s worth asking the priest or minister what is allowed during the service. A QR code on the order of service reminds guests to send their photos right afterwards, at their own pace.

m2.d: A card on each table or beside the party favors: between courses come the most natural shots, of the cousins, of grandparents holding the baby, of the cake.

m3.d: People who came a long way often have the best photos and the least time to send them. A QR code on the table and a link in the family group chat turn it into a few seconds’ job.

m4.d: A christening gets talked about for weeks: if an uncle or a grandparent hasn’t sent anything yet, a message with the same link is all it takes to remind them while the album is open. There is always a “forgotten” photo on someone’s phone.

i1.t: Photos and videos from the whole family
i1.d: The album takes videos too (up to {videoMax} MB each) and plays them in the gallery.

i2.d: A page opens in the phone’s browser, easy enough for grandparents. A name is optional.

i3.d: We keep every photo and video exactly as it was sent: the album shows lighter copies, downloading gives you the original.

i4.d: With the Full album you download every original in a single click.

i5.d: Only people with the QR code or the link can take part. In the privacy settings you choose whether guests can upload and whether photos appear on the screen.

i6.d: Your album stays yours for 365 days from activation. Download the originals before it ends: after that, the content is deleted.

price.text: The trial is free for 7 days, needs no credit card (one per account) and holds up to {trialLimit} photos and videos in total: for a christening with a small guest list that can be enough. After the 7 days new uploads stop. To keep going, and to get the ZIP, printable cards and no MIOLOVE mark, activate the Full album: {price} as a single payment per album, valid for 365 days, with no cap on guests or on the album’s total. No monthly fee and no charge per guest.

q1.q: Can guests use the QR code during the service in church?
q1.a: The QR code matters most after the service. During the ceremony it’s best to ask the priest or minister what is allowed, and to invite guests to send photos and videos afterwards, at the lunch.

q2.q: Will the grandparents know what to do?
q2.a: Give them the simplest job: point the camera at the QR code printed on the table and tap the send button on the page that opens. There is nothing to download or sign up for, and a grandchild can help in seconds.

q3.q: Can I collect the photos from the days around the christening too?
q3.a: Yes. The album stays open for as long as it is active, so you can gather the photos of the preparations, the dressing of the baby or the party at the grandparents’ house as well as the ceremony.

q4.q: Is the free trial enough for a christening?
q4.a: For a christening with a small guest list the trial (up to {trialLimit} photos and videos, 7 days) can be enough. Keeping everything longer, downloading the ZIP and printing the cards need the Full album, where each guest can send up to {guestCap} files (an anti-spam ceiling).

q5.q: How long are the christening photos kept?
q5.a: An active album stays yours for 365 days from activation. Before it ends, download the originals as one ZIP and save them with the family photos; after that, the content is deleted.
